page_title: Arm’s Neoverse V2, in AWS’s Graviton 4

sources.entry: Arm's Neoverse V2, in AWS's Graviton 4 - Measures a sustained rename width below the stated one, cache latencies, mesh behaviour and cross-socket cost on V2.

summary.title: Arm's Neoverse V2, in AWS's Graviton 4
summary.one_liner: A detailed microarchitecture and measurement look at Arm's Neoverse V2 core and its 96-core, dual-socket implementation in AWS Graviton 4, covering latency, bandwidth, front end, renamer, backend and load/store behaviour compared with AMD Zen 4 and Intel Golden Cove.
keywords: arm vs amd vs intel server cpu
how wide is neoverse v2 renamer
why is graviton 4 slower than zen 4
takeaways: Graviton 4 pairs 96 Neoverse V2 cores on a CMN-700 mesh; dual-socket instances reach 192 cores, with cross-socket latency around 138.6 ns and cross-socket bandwidth just over 77 GB/s.
The author measured a sustained rename width of about 6 micro-ops per cycle, below Arm's stated 8, making V2 effectively a 6-wide core.
Neoverse V2 has a 64 KB L1D, a 2 MB L2 with 11-cycle latency, and an L3 hit near 25 ns, while running at low clocks (up to 2.8 GHz, 2.7 GHz dual socket).
In the author's tests, V2 had higher IPC than Zen 4 but lower overall performance in libx264 and 7-Zip because of lower clocks and no SMT advantage.
Store forwarding is limited on V2 (only halves of a 64-bit store forward to a 32-bit load), which the author compares to Neoverse N1 and says is weaker than Intel and AMD.
summary.summary: The article examines AWS Graviton 4, which uses 96 Arm Neoverse V2 cores, first covering system-level latency and bandwidth on the CMN-700 mesh, DRAM and dual-socket configurations. It then walks through the V2 core: branch prediction, front end and micro-op cache, rename, out-of-order scheduling, FP/vector pipes, load/store unit, TLBs and caches. The author uses microbenchmarks and performance counters, and compares results with AMD Zen 4, Bergamo, Genoa-X and Intel Golden Cove. The article ends with libx264 and 7-Zip runs against Zen 4 to show how the design choices play out in practice.
